gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Jabees sells two 7Seven models: the 7Seven Air at $49.99 with 8 GB of MP3 memory, and the 7Seven at $59.99 on Jabees' own store. That explains why ChatGPT saw '8 GB vs 32 GB' listings, and the 7Seven costs well below the $74–80 ChatGPT quoted.
standout_why: SoundMavericks (cited in chat 3) already lists depth and time limits and file formats for the Shokz OpenSwim Pro (2 m for 2 h), Shokz OpenSwim (2 m for 2 h), FINIS Duo (3 m for 30 min), PSIER S18 (2 m for 1 h) and Nank Diver2 Pro (IP69, no depth given). It has no depth or time for the MOJAWA Run Plus or the Jabees 7Seven, and those are ChatGPT's two top picks. ChatGPT itself warned that 7Seven 'storage listings vary'. I couldn't read WIRED, TechRadar or Verywell Fit (fetch blocked or truncated), so I can't rule out that they cover the split between the 7Seven and the 7Seven Air. Our angle found only part of the answer, because I couldn't open the 7Seven and Run Plus spec pages (Shopify returned HTTP 429 on every product page).
decides: It confirms the Jabees 7Seven as the value pick, at $59.99 direct rather than ~$75. It also tells the page to name the exact model: the $49.99 7Seven Air has only 8 GB. The H2O SONAR that ChatGPT priced at $99.99 shows up on H2O's store only as the SONAR 2 PRO at $149.99, which is over the $100 budget, so it should drop out unless the original SONAR is shown in stock at $99.99. The normalised water-rating table favours H2O's 3.6 m with no time limit over the 2 m/1–2 h and 3 m/30 min ratings. That doesn't change the under-$100 pick, because H2O's only sub-$100 MP3 product is the STREAM 3 PRO, a goggle-strap player that takes separate SURGE headphones. Fix our current page: H2O's store lists the TRI 2 PRO at $219.99 with 4 GB, not 8 GB at $199.99.
